project.name: Ledgerline
project.goal: A web app that turns a freelancer's raw bank CSV export into a categorized income/expense ledger.
project.primary_user: A solo freelancer who dreads sorting a quarter's transactions before filing taxes.
project.core_problem: Bank CSV exports are flat and uncategorized; freelancers currently hand-sort hundreds of rows in a spreadsheet before every filing.
project.core_journey:
1. The freelancer uploads a bank CSV export.
2. The app categorizes each transaction and flags anything it cannot confidently place.
3. The freelancer confirms or recategorizes flagged rows and exports a clean ledger.
project.success_measure: A freelancer produces a confirmed, exportable ledger from a raw CSV in under ten minutes, down from an afternoon.
project.success_metrics:
- time to exported ledger -- under 10 minutes
- rows requiring manual recategorization -- under 10% on the reference export
project.riskiest_assumption: A rules-based categorizer can place most transactions correctly without needing an LLM in the loop.
project.req_ac_list:
- [ ] **REQ-AC1:** Uploading a CSV yields a categorized ledger with low-confidence rows visibly flagged.
- [ ] **REQ-AC2:** Confirming or recategorizing a flagged row updates the ledger and clears the flag.
- [ ] **REQ-AC3:** Exporting produces a CSV with every row's final category.
project.non_goals:
- No bank API integrations in the first iteration; CSV upload only.
- No multi-currency support; single-currency ledgers only.
project.constraint_time: Four weeks to a usable first version.
project.constraint_cost: No paid services; the categorizer must run without any external API calls.
project.constraint_data: Bank exports may contain account numbers; uploads are processed in memory and never written to disk.
project.deployment_target: Static SPA hosted on the freelancer's own infra.
project.scale_expectations: Single user per deployment, a few uploads per month.
project.in_scope_list:
- CSV upload and rules-based categorization.
- Low-confidence flagging and manual recategorization.
- Clean CSV export of the final ledger.
project.pain_point: dreads sorting a quarter's transactions before filing taxes
project.key_benefit: categorizes automatically and only asks about what it is unsure of
project.key_differentiator: low-confidence rows are flagged instead of silently miscategorized

positive_reference.ref: the clean tabular editing of airtable.com

design.references:
- airtable.com -- dense tabular editing that stays legible at speed
- linear.app -- calm density, restrained color, keyboard-first affordances
design.anti_reference: generic spreadsheet clone: default browser table styling, no visual hierarchy, red/green the only signal

features.title: Upload and categorize a CSV
features.intent: Uploading a CSV yields a categorized ledger with low-confidence rows visibly flagged.
features.serves: journey step 2: the app categorizes each transaction and flags anything it cannot confidently place
acceptance: Uploading a sample CSV produces a ledger where every row has a category and low-confidence rows are visibly flagged.

features.title: Recategorize a flagged row
features.intent: Confirming or recategorizing a flagged row updates the ledger and clears the flag.
features.serves: journey step 3: the freelancer confirms or recategorizes flagged rows and exports a clean ledger
acceptance: Recategorizing a flagged row updates its category and removes the flag from the ledger view.

features.title: Export the final ledger
features.intent: Exporting produces a CSV with every row's final category.
features.serves: differentiator: low-confidence rows are flagged instead of silently miscategorized
acceptance: Exporting after confirming all flags produces a downloadable CSV with a category on every row.
